children: heads into a high-stakes Investor Day on September 23 with shares down more than 16% this year and investors looking for evidence that management can revive U.S. traffic without sacrificing franchisee economics. The event could reset expectations for 2027 and beyond, with Wall Street focused on store remodel spending, unit growth, digital monetization and whether the company's emerging beverage platform can become a meaningful new growth engine.

Deutsche Bank analyst Lauren Silberman expects McDonald's to provide select 2027 financial targets alongside longer-term goals for 2028 through 2030 and additional details on its McDonald's > NEXT growth and productivity strategy.

"We believe the most anticipated area of focus is around MCD's partnering contribution for the upcoming 10-year US remodel cycle and what that means for incremental capex over the next several years," Silberman wrote.

That spending question matters because McDonald's may need to balance restaurant upgrades against global expansion and franchisee returns. Deutsche Bank sees potential moderation in unit-growth expectations as capital requirements rise and refranchising activity increases.
Traffic could be an even bigger issue.

RBC Capital Markets analyst Logan Reich said investor interest in restaurant stocks remains depressed amid macro pressure on same-store sales and believes McDonald's needs comparable-sales growth to reaccelerate before sentiment meaningfully improves, potentially around the first quarter of 2027.
The company's new beverage platform will also be closely watched after launches in the U.S., Canada and Germany reportedly exceeded expectations.
"On beverages, we expect an update on the pace of international expansion, where the majority of global markets could get the platform soon," Reich said.
Investor Day needs to deliver more than ambitious long-term goals.
Investors should watch 2027 sales and margin targets, planned remodel spending, franchisee contributions, unit-growth expectations and concrete plans for restoring U.S. traffic.
Morgan Stanley's Brian Harbour cautions that higher spending and long implementation timelines could limit the event's immediate earnings impact.
"We think investors will want to see proof points for some of the initiatives and see numbers start to move higher again, as do we to become outright constructive," Harbour said.

A credible traffic recovery plan and stronger beverage economics could improve sentiment. Higher capital requirements without faster same-store sales growth would make the stock's recovery considerably harder.

title: McDonald's Investors Brace for Major Update
